text:
Parker Wotherspoon came to Vegas from Pittsburgh, played the first four games of October, then missed a month before returning on Nov. 11. He has played about 18 minutes a night since.

He doesn't score and isn't asked to: one assist and no goals in 12 games, on 12 shots. Our comparisons put him next to Brian Dumoulin and Jonas Siegenthaler, defensemen who shoot rarely. Last season's 27 assists in Pittsburgh look like the high end of what he does.

The five-on-five work is the good news. Vegas takes 59.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about seven points better than without him, and the team has scored 3.9 fewer goals than those chances deserve during his shifts, a gap that usually closes. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.0 wins above replacement last season, 72nd among 215 defensemen.

One blemish came in the second Dallas game, when The Athletic's Jesse Granger wrote of Thomas Harley's tying goal: "I'm not really sure why Wotherspoon was swinging his stick at it." Watch whether his minutes hold through December.
